cold_scope: Two newly materialized and hash-verified target executable copies followed by paired reuse; no claim of OS page-cache eviction.
failure_policy: No per-case retry. Any failed report, timeout, exit, cleanup, hash or series completeness check invalidates the host cell; retain attempts and require a declared replacement.
harness_hash_policy: Hash staged Git index blob bytes; for .py, .ps1, .yml and .yaml normalize CRLF to LF before SHA-256. Runtime worktree files are normalized identically before comparison.
original_failures: Preserve all v1/v2 hosted startup and Unicode failures plus the v3 Linux PTY bridge failure; catalog v3/source development then passed and was independently audited. A native local Windows exact-candidate preflight was refused before target launch because the deep workspace path returned Access is denied; standard hosted Windows is the declared final host.

retention.native_binary_payload_policy: Retain exact original candidate reference and byte hash; never duplicate full provider archives.

scenario_alias_policy: Materialize host-contracts/scenarios.json as an exact byte copy of frozen scenarios-native-exit-v6.json, verify its SHA-256, and record the alias digest in the host contract freeze before the final journal reads it.
scope: Exact v0.4.0-rc.6 native-exit-v1 final execution only. Independent report/fault/source/runtime audit, old-project requalification, retention and confirmed cleanup remain required before admission.
source_archive_policy: Generated locally as deterministic gzip/PAX from the verified pinned checkout; the archive is reopened and every member SHA-256 is checked against source-provenance.json before build. The generated archive digest and bytes are bound in acquisition.json and the execution plan.

supersedes.reason: Run 41970500610 launched 432 target cases: Windows passed 240 cases and nine source-fault phases, with checked cleanup. Linux passed 191 cases then N14 was cancelled after 3.65 seconds in loaded batch 9; the preceding nine full batches passed. Both hosts restored source/runtime and completed checked removal. V12 gives all frozen cases a 20-second step and 60-second run bound. The attempt remains zero-credit. V12 did not launch any target cases: final-series preflight still looked up the v5 scenario alias after the frozen inputs advanced to v6. Both cleanup jobs refused deletion without target-report evidence; Windows independently confirmed no live target process. V13 completed 240 Windows cases plus nine fault phases, while Linux passed 195 cases before the outer next20_check deadline cancelled N18 at exactly 1200 seconds. Both hosts restored and checked removal. V14 raises the outer bound to 2400 seconds under the existing 60-minute job limit and binds the workflow source in its harness hashes. V14 workflow 41978773971 requested a 2400-second command deadline, but the next20_check adapter rejected it at its 1200-second parser cap before any target launch on either host. Both refusal packets and zero-launch cleanup refusals are preserved; target case counters do not change. V15 raises the adapter cap with numeric argument validation and boundary coverage. V15 run 41980469906 passed Windows 240 ordinary cases and all nine fault phases with process/source/runtime cleanup. Linux passed 220 ordinary cases in batches 0-10; its first batch-11 N01 launch produced no initial output within the declared 2000 ms startup boundary and failed with assertion_timeout. The attempt, report and both host packets are retained; no retry or candidate credit is counted. V16 changes only the Linux batch-11 startup boundary to 5000 ms based on this observed timeout; Windows remains 2000 ms and ordinary deadlines are unchanged. V16 run 41984301547 confirmed Linux again materialized N01 with a 2000 ms startup deadline despite its declared 5000 ms value. The shared batch runner read its legacy v1 declaration because Git Town had validated v16 only in the top-level wrapper. Windows completed its full 240-case/nine-phase series and checked cleanup; Linux passed 220 cases before the same first-output timeout. Preserve the attempt without retry credit. V17 threads the selected candidate host profile explicitly into the shared batch runner, with a regression proving the explicit value overrides the legacy profile. V17 run 41988031958 fixed the Linux generated contract at the declared 5000 ms, but its batch-11 N01 startup still timed out at 5040 ms with exit 130; the target process and workspace were cleaned. All ten preceding Linux N01 reports passed, each taking about 5050-5067 ms for the first expected output, so v18 raises only this declared startup edge boundary to 6000 ms. The ordinary 20 s step and 60 s run limits do not change. Windows passed 240 cases and nine fault phases. The v17 artifact omitted active case-evidence, fault-build, and mutated-binary records, so its fault matrix cannot be independently audited; v18 includes those bounded paths.
